text:
Maria G: Customer (FinLit) opened an escalation — streaming responses keep cutting off mid-token, client sees partial JSON and then reconnects. Happening ~10-15% of requests, mostly on their prod region us-east-1. They say it started after they put a gRPC->HTTP1 gateway in front of our API.

Maria G: Example from customer: they get a few SSE chunks then connection drops. They attempt an EventSource reconnect and get the remainder sometimes, sometimes not. They shared one request id: req_01F8X2ABCDNQ2

support-bot: Incident INC-2026-114 created for request req_01F8X2ABCDNQ2 — priority P1 (streaming degraded)

Kevin T: Can you share a minimal repro curl command that they used? Also need any gateway/proxy config. Do we have backend logs for that request id?

Maria G: They provided this curl repro:

```
curl -v --http2 -N \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate/stream?model=gpt-open" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream"
```

Maria G: Their gateway is envoy + a custom http1 adapter that translates downstream http2 to upstream http1. They suspect the adapter buffers chunks until a newline or buffer full.

Alex R: If there's a translation h2->h1, chunking semantics can get lost. SSE relies on timely chunk flushes. Many h2->h1 proxies will wait for a TCP flush or fill a buffer before sending out a chunk. That matches "partial outputs" + reconnect behavior.

Ingrid P: Do we see any RST_STREAM or GOAWAY in our logs for that request id? The customer's capture suggests an RST coming from the proxy (not from our runtime). Example lines they pasted:

```
[envoy] connection ended: code=RST_STREAM, id=5
client: EOF
```

Kevin T: Ok pls attach the full proxy logs. Meanwhile, try two quick repros from our side:
1) curl --http2 -N (h2 path)
2) curl --http1.1 -N (force http1 path)

Samir V: I tried a local repro with an nginx reverse proxy that has `proxy_buffering on` by default — I saw identical truncation. Disabling buffering and enabling chunked transfer fixed it in my test.

Alex R: Shared practical nginx tweaks that often help (customer's adapter may use similar buffering):

```
# nginx reverse proxy (example)
location /v1/generate/stream {
  proxy_buffering off;
  proxy_http_version 1.1;        # keep upstream as http1.1 if translating
  proxy_set_header Connection ""; # avoid forcing keep-alive header rewrite
  chunked_transfer_encoding on;
}
```

Ingrid P: For Envoy-based converters, look at `stream_idle_timeout`, `max_stream_duration`, and `http1_protocol_options` — some adapters coalesce data to satisfy http1 framing.

Maria G: Customer said their adapter team set `enable_coalescing: true` to reduce small packets, but that causes long pauses. They're rolling that back for a test.

Kevin T: Also ask them to do a tcpdump (pcap) on the gateway for one failing request. We need to confirm who sends the RST: client, gateway, or our edge. If gateway is buffering, we'll see large delays between data frames.

Samir V: One more thing: SSE over HTTP/2 is safe but some intermediate gateways terminate HTTP/2 and reserialize into chunked HTTP/1. If the gateway waits to accumulate N bytes before writing a chunk, the SSE data is held back. Reconnects happen when gateway or client tcp timeouts trigger.

Maria G: They ran both tests. Results:
- http2->our-edge->client (no intermediary) = stable
- http2->gateway->http1->client = flaky (most truncations)

Alex R: That squarely points to the gateway translation layer. Workarounds:
- Ask gateway team to disable buffering/coalescing for streaming routes
- If possible, keep end-to-end HTTP/2 (passthrough) so no translation occurs
- If translation unavoidable, have adapter flush after every SSE event (or set a very small chunk size)

Ingrid P: Also check TCP keepalive and proxy idle timeouts. Some gateways close idle streams after Xs and our runtime keeps sending but the connection is dead.

Kevin T: For immediate customer workaround, suggest:
1) Use longpoll with poll_interval 500ms if they can tolerate latency
2) Use non-streaming API (streaming=false) and poll for partial results
3) Configure gateway to be streaming-friendly (preferred)

Maria G: I asked customer to collect a pcap and core logs. They attached a small snippet of netstat showing many CLOSE_WAIT on the gateway side.

Samir V: CLOSE_WAIT indicates the peer didn't fully close the socket — could be their adapter failing to finish the TCP close, or app-level crash. That would align with partial output + stale connection state.

Alex R: Action items for eng-runtime:
- Enable debug logging for request req_01F8X2ABCDNQ2 timeframe, include HTTP/2 frame logs (SYN/SETTINGS/HEADERS/DATA/RESET)
- Check where RST_STREAM originates (our edge or remote proxy)
- If originating at our side, capture kernel-level trace (tcpdump + strace on edge process)

Ingrid P: Assigning to @Kevin T to coordinate with the customer's gateway team. @Alex R and @Samir V to validate proxy config suggestions.

Kevin T: I'll reach out to customer gateway engineers and request pcap, envoy/nginx config, and the adapter repo/version. Also asked them to try `curl --http2 --no-buffer -N` and to flip coalescing off.

Maria G: Customer will provide pcap + config by EOD. Marking this thread for follow-up. Thanks all :pray:

support-bot: INC-2026-114 updated: awaiting customer pcap + gateway logs

Alex R: Quick note for docs: we should add a short KB titled "Streaming + intermediaries (h2->h1) — common pitfalls" with sample proxy configs and curl repro. I'll draft once we confirm root cause.

Kevin T: Leaving this for now. If we see the RST from our edge I'll ping in #eng-runtime. Otherwise I'll update.

Maria G: Closing loop: customer reported rollback of coalescing flag reduced failures to <1%. Keeping open until pcap reviewed.
